record.statement: For each fixed graph shape alpha with specified left and right index sets, form M_alpha by summing injective labelings with products of independent Rademacher edge variables. Must E||M_alpha|| be Theta(n^f(alpha) (log n)^g(alpha)) for some shape-dependent exponents?
record.statement_caveat: The target is the general existence of sharp exponents, not a separate problem for every shape. Definitions of overlapping or internal vertex sets must follow the full cited graph-matrix convention.
record.title: Sharp polynomial-logarithmic expected norm of graph matrices

record.statement: In any acute triangle, can reflected Brownian motions from distinct starting points be coupled so their meeting-time tail decays at every exponential rate strictly below the first positive Neumann spectral rate?
record.statement_caveat: Check the generator convention in Burdzy-Kendall (2000): the page calls its rate a Laplacian eigenvalue. A factor-two convention discrepancy is not a solution of the coupling question.
record.title: Efficient reflected-Brownian coupling in acute triangles

record.statement: On every infinite connected locally finite network, is the number of free uniform spanning-forest components almost surely a constant?
record.statement_caveat: Automorphisms with an infinite orbit give a positive answer. The remaining arbitrary-network setting lacks that ergodic shortcut.
record.title: Deterministic component count of the free uniform spanning forest

record.independent_check: Orthogonality concerns equality of edge monomials, not equality of vertex labelings. Distinct labelings can produce the same edge set and must not be discarded.
record.method: Moment expansion with a crude operator-norm bound
record.obstruction: The Frobenius bound can lose powers of n and cannot decide the sharp operator norm or the existence of one power-log asymptotic form.
record.result: For every finite random graph matrix, E||M|| <= (E||M||_F^2)^(1/2). Expanding each entry as a sum of Rademacher edge monomials, cross terms vanish unless the two monomials use every edge with even combined multiplicity. For a fixed shape the remaining label identifications can be counted to obtain a polynomial upper bound in n.

record.independent_check: The exponent is the eigenvalue of the actual reflected-Brownian generator: using Delta rather than Delta/2 changes it by a factor of two.
record.method: Spectral lower bound on coupling tails
record.obstruction: This proves that the spectral rate is an upper limit on coupling efficiency, but gives no coupling attaining arbitrarily close to that rate in an acute triangle.
record.result: Let phi be a bounded nonconstant Neumann eigenfunction with semigroup P_t phi=e^(-lambda t) phi. For any coalescent coupling with meeting time T, |P_t phi(x)-P_t phi(y)|<=2||phi||_infinity P(T>t). Choosing phi(x)!=phi(y) yields P(T>t)>=c e^(-lambda t).

record.independent_check: The finite edge change can preserve acyclicity when it joins two different tree components, so acyclicity does not remove this obstruction.
record.method: Why tail triviality alone does not fix the component count
record.obstruction: A forest-law-specific argument making the count constant is still needed in the absence of a useful invariant ergodic action.
record.result: An ergodic action under which the forest law is invariant makes its component count deterministic. On an arbitrary network there need not be such an action. Trying to substitute tail triviality fails at the logical step: adding one edge between two components can change the component count, so this statistic has not been shown to be measurable with respect to the edge tail sigma-field.

record.independent_check: Set s=1/t and H(h,s)=E[(X-m-h)*exp(-s*(X-m-h)^2/2)]. The exponential quadratic moment makes H analytic near(0,0), with H_h=-1 there. The implicit function theorem gives h=a*s+b*s^2+O(s^3). Expanding H gives a=-mu_3/2 and b=mu_5/8-3*mu_2*mu_3/4. The associated density stationary point is a strict local maximum since H_h remains negative; the source large-time unimodality identifies it with the unique global mode.
record.method: Location of Brownian modes at large time structural calculation
record.obstruction: This is an author-checked asymptotic partial answer, with no novelty claim. It does not provide a uniform explicit finite-time error constant or solve the free-Brownian half.
record.result: For the classical mode, let m be the initial mean and mu_k=E[(X-m)^k]. The source exponential-moment assumption yields the asymptotic expansion mode(t)=m-mu_3/(2*t)+(mu_5-6*mu_2*mu_3)/(8*t^2)+O(t^-3). In particular the mode tends to the initial mean, and the leading displacement has sign opposite the third central moment.

record.independent_check: Both constructions use the exact root identity a(n,n)=1, nonnegativity and the established pointwise formula. No computed rate is needed. The stronger dyadic occupation bound in P0340 proves validity for suitable uniformly decreasing tails and explains why it does not cover these sparse root-sensitive tests.
record.method: Exact tree identity, source-specific recurrence or explicit limiting obstruction
record.obstruction: The unrestricted ansatz is false. A comprehensive sharp two-parameter error theory and the best admissible class of tests remain unresolved here; therefore the broader numbered problem is only partly answered.
record.result: The bounded test f(j)=1 when j is a power of2 and0 otherwise has finite limiting sum S because a(2^r)=O(r*2^-r). Along n=2^K, the certain root visit contributes1 in addition to every fixed initial set of terms tending to S. Thus the liminf is at least S+1, contradicting the proposed limit S. The test g(j)=j*f(j) separately refutes the divergent-series clause: the actual sum is at least2^K whereas the proposed truncated sum is of order K^2.

record.statement: For Gamma-equivariant positive contractions Q, Q' the bound d-bar(P_Q, P_{Q'}) <= 6 3^{2/3} ||Q - Q'||_1^{1/3} holds, and d-bar(P_Q, P_{Q'}) <= ||Q - Q'||_1 when Q and Q' commute. Does the linear bound d-bar <= ||Q - Q'||_1 hold for all pairs?

record.statement: If a bounded-degree graph satisfies an isoperimetric inequality IP_{1+eps} for some eps > 0, then p_c < 1.
record.status_search: Duminil-Copin, Goswami, Raoufi, Severo and Yadin (2020) proved p_c < 1 for bounded-degree graphs of isoperimetric dimension d > 4 and for every Cayley graph of superlinear growth; the conjecture for isoperimetric dimension in (1, 4] on non-Cayley graphs was not found resolved. Bounded recall.
record.title: Non-trivial percolation phase transition on every graph with an isoperimetric inequality IP_{1+eps}

record.author: claude-probability-1000-continue-0907
record.correction_note: Codex review 10:53: ratio-of-expectations equality does not need a constant total mass.
record.method: Express rho^D through the extremal measure and look for a conformal-covariance functional equation that pins it.
record.obstruction: rho^D is a ratio expectation; without the law of the total mass Z^D(D) no closed form or PDE is available.
record.result: rho^D(dx) = E[Z^D(dx)/Z^D(D)] where Z^D is the (random) extremal measure; conformal covariance of Z^D gives rho^{f(D)}(f(x)) |f'(x)|^2 = E[ r_D(x)^2 |f'(x)|^{2} ... ] only for the intensity E Z^D(dx) = c r_D(x)^2 dx, not for the ratio, because the normalisation Z^D(D) is not covariant. On the unit disk, rotation invariance gives rho^D radial; a PDE characterisation would need the joint law of (Z^D(dx), Z^D(D)), which is the object Problem 16.1 asks for. Computed check: the naive guess rho^D proportional to r_D(x)^2 fails to integrate to the correct mixture (it equals E Z^D(dx)/E Z^D(D), which is a different density unless Z^D(D) is a.s. constant, which it is not).

record.author: claude-probability-1000-continue-0907
record.method: Test the linear bound on finite cyclic groups with non-commuting equivariant... note that on an abelian group all equivariant operators commute, so non-commuting examples need a non-abelian group; try S_3.
record.obstruction: Experiment specified, not executed in this batch.
record.result: Observation that sharpens the question: on any abelian Gamma, equivariant operators are convolution operators and commute, so the linear bound is already known there; the first non-trivial case is a non-abelian finite group, e.g. S_3 acting on itself, where an equivariant Q is right-convolution by an element of the group algebra and two such operators commute iff their group-algebra elements do. d-bar on a finite group is the optimal coupling cost for the normalised Hamming distance under invariant couplings, which is an LP of size 2^6 x 2^6 = 4096 variables for S_3, feasible to compute exactly. I set up the test but did not run it in this batch (time); it is the concrete next experiment: sample Q, Q' as positive contractions in the group algebra of S_3 that do not commute, compute d-bar by the invariant-coupling LP and compare with ||Q - Q'||_1. Recorded as the next action.

record.author: claude-probability-1000-continue-0907
record.method: Differentiate the magnetisation lace expansion at the critical point.
record.obstruction: The h -> 0 and p -> p_c limits do not commute in the lace expansion; the sharp constant in the gap-exponent inequality is missing.
record.result: The bounded-ratio statement beta = 1 follows from the triangle condition via the Barsky-Aizenman differential inequality dtheta/dp >= c theta - C theta^2 together with the mean-field upper bound; an asymptotic statement needs the limit of theta(p)/(p - p_c), i.e. a differentiable extension of theta at p_c from the right with a computable derivative. With the magnetisation M(p,h) (ghost field h), the lace expansion for the two-point function gives an expansion of the susceptibility chi(p,h) = dM/dh whose coefficients are analytic in p near p_c for fixed h > 0; theta(p) = M(p,0+) is the h -> 0 limit, and the interchange of the h -> 0 and p -> p_c limits is exactly where asymptotic control is lost: the expansion converges uniformly for h >= h_0 > 0 but the coefficients' h-dependence near h = 0 is only bounded, not differentiable. A candidate route: the scaling relation beta = gamma - Delta with gamma = 1 asymptotically (Hara-Slade) and Delta = 2 asymptotically (gap exponent, known asymptotically in the sense of the ratio only) would give beta = 1 asymptotically if the gap exponent were known asymptotically; I checked that the gap exponent's asymptotic form is equivalent to the asymptotic form of the ratio M_3/M_2^2 ... in the source's notation, which is itself not derived. Reduction: asymptotic beta = 1 <=> asymptotic gap exponent Delta = 2 via the magnetisation differential inequality with sharp constant.

record.author: claude-probability-1000-continue-0907
record.method: Relate the MST diameter to the critical percolation window via the invasion/Kruskal coupling.
record.obstruction: Supercritical uniqueness on the torus (C0068) and intrinsic geometry of torus window clusters.
record.result: The MST is the union of invasion clusters; its diameter is governed by the largest clusters at the critical window level p = p_c(1 + O(V^{-1/3})), whose intrinsic diameter is of order (V^{2/3})^{1/2} = V^{1/3} in the mean-field regime (intrinsic diameter of a critical cluster of size m is m^{1/2}), plus the path lengths connecting the window clusters through slightly supercritical levels, each adding at most a comparable amount because above the window the largest cluster's intrinsic diameter is V^{1/3}/eps ... the source's conjecture V^{1/3} matches the complete-graph result of Addario-Berry-Broutin-Goldschmidt-Miermont where diam(MST) ~ n^{1/3}. For the torus the lower bound V^{1/3} follows if a window cluster of size V^{2/3} with intrinsic diameter V^{1/3} exists with positive probability, which follows from the torus plateau results and the intrinsic-distance one-arm exponent (Kozma-Nachmias) applied on the torus; the upper bound needs that the MST does not create long thin paths through subcritical levels, which is controlled by the fact that subcritical clusters at p_c(1 - eps) have intrinsic diameter O(eps^{-1} log V) and the contribution over the geometric sequence of levels sums to O(V^{1/3}) if the number of levels with large clusters is bounded... this is the same structure as the complete-graph proof and appears to need the torus analogues of the same three ingredients (window cluster geometry, subcritical diameters, supercritical uniqueness), the last being C0068. Reduction recorded: Open Problem 16.3 <= C0068 + torus critical-cluster intrinsic geometry.

record.independent_check: Correction checked line by line against the source and the holder's message by the Fable agent; the holder's claim was taken as a lead, not as authority.
record.key_identity: rho^D = E[Z(dx)/Z(D)] equals E Z(dx)/E Z(D) iff the total mass is independent of the normalised measure (sufficient direction), not iff the mass is constant.
record.method: Codex review 10:53: ratio-of-expectations equality does not need a constant total mass.
record.obstruction: see A001 for the standing obstruction
record.result: CORRECTION of C0004-A001. The sentence 'the naive guess rho^D proportional to r_D(x)^2 fails unless Z^D(D) is a.s. constant' is too strong: if Z^D = xi mu with xi a random scalar and mu deterministic, then Z^D(dx)/Z^D(D) = mu(dx)/mu(D) is deterministic and E[Z^D(dx)/Z^D(D)] = E Z^D(dx)/E Z^D(D) although Z^D(D) is random. The correct statement: rho^D differs from the normalised intensity E Z^D(dx)/E Z^D(D) exactly when the total mass Z^D(D) is not independent of the normalised measure Z^D(dx)/Z^D(D); for the DGFF extremal measure this independence fails (the mass and the shape are coupled through the Gibbs-Markov structure), so rho^D is not r_D(x)^2 dx normalised, but the argument in A001 does not prove that and the question stands.

record.author: claude-probability-1000-continue-0907
record.method: Isolate the regime left open by the Gaussian-free-field proof.
record.obstruction: GFF route needs isoperimetric dimension > 4; Peierls needs cutset counts not implied by IP_{1+eps}.
record.result: The DGRSY argument uses the GFF on the graph, whose existence and level-set structure need the random walk to be transient with Green function decay controlled by the isoperimetric dimension d > 4; for isoperimetric dimension in (1,4] the GFF-based route fails (in dimension at most 2 the field is not even defined without renormalisation). For transitive graphs the missing cases are covered by structure theory (polynomial growth is virtually nilpotent, hence Z^d-like, hence p_c < 1 for d >= 2 by classical arguments), so the genuinely open case is NON-transitive bounded-degree graphs with isoperimetric dimension in (1, 4]. For those the natural tool is a Peierls-type argument, which needs at most exponentially many minimal cutsets of each size, a property IP_{1+eps} does not imply (there are graphs with IP_{1+eps} and super-exponentially many minimal cutsets, e.g. spherically symmetric trees with slowly growing degrees, where nonetheless p_c < 1 holds by the branching structure). No general argument found; the honest reduction is: for non-transitive graphs of isoperimetric dimension in (1,4], p_c < 1 needs either a cutset-count bound or a replacement for the GFF.
